subject: RFP: metering, prepay credits & overage structure - HealthSys

Subject: RFP Q: metering unit, prepay credits, overage mechanics (HealthSys RFP)

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the materials you sent last week. The RFP review team has a few clarifying questions on the commercial section before we include Redwood in our short list. For brevity we numbered them below — a short written response is fine, attachment preferred if you have a sample pricing table.

1) Metering unit: does Redwood meter per model-inferred token (output-only), total tokens (prompt + output), or by request? Please confirm default for hosted API and how Dedicated differs.
2) Commit mechanics: are commits quoted monthly or annually? Do unused commit credits roll? Is there a quarterly true-up?
3) Prepay / credits: can we prepay and receive a bonus (e.g., 10% liquidity)? Are credits tied to account or to a specific project/org?
4) Overage calculation: what is the overage rate if monthly usage exceeds commit? Any stair-step bands or escalating rates? How do burst allowances integrate with overage billing?
5) Discounts & marketplace: how do marketplace fees or reseller channels affect list price? Any pass-throughs/adjustments?
6) Billing & invoicing: Net terms, currency, and typical invoice timing for committed customers.
7) SLA credits: are SLA credits (latency / availability) applied as financial offsets to monthly invoices?

Can you return a compact pricing proposal (table + short narrative) by COB Thu 20 Aug? We plan to review and set a 30-min follow-up if needed.

Best,
Amit Shah
Procurement Manager
HealthSys Inc.

Team — forwarding HealthSys' questions (see below). They want a compact pricing proposal by COB Thu. High priority.

Notes / constraints to consider when drafting:
- They are a regulated healthcare org; likely want Private or Dedicated options for PHI workloads. Pricing should show parity across hosted/dedicated with explicit delta for private networking & KMS.
- Emphasize liquidity on prepay (they asked specifically) and allow cross-project credit pooling (we call this "liquid credit pool").
- Include a stair-step overage model that protects from bill shocks but disincentivizes perpetual overuse versus commits.
- Show explicit accounting for marketplace/reseller fees (we should show both list and net to Redwood).

Ben — can you draft the numbers (token tiers + prepay bonus + overage ladder)? Marissa — add recommended contractual language for quarterly true-up, 30-day billing, and SLA offsets. Dylan — include ops notes on Dedicated burst allowances and how we meter KV cache vs tokens.

I will review and send to HealthSys.

Lauren — draft numbers below (quick pass). I focused on a clean, defensible structure we can defend vs enterprise peer comps. I'll format into the Excel template and attach.

Pricing assumptions (hosted, USD):
- Metering: default = prompt + generated tokens (total tokens). For Dedicated, same token semantics but usage ties to reserved GPU capacity; bursts consume burst allowance and then overage credits.

Token pricing (list, per-token; billed per 1k tokens in invoices):
- Base open model (text-gen): $0.60 / 1K tokens
- Fine-tuned / custom model: $1.20 / 1K tokens
- Embeddings: $0.18 / 1K tokens

Commit tiers (monthly committed spend / effective per-1k rate after commit discounts):
- 0 - 5M tokens: list rates apply (no commit)
- 5M - 50M tokens: 15% commit discount
- 50M - 250M tokens: 30% commit discount
- >250M tokens: 40% commit discount + optional reserved capacity pricing (sustained throughput SLA)

Prepay credits: 10% bonus liquidity for prepay >= 6 months equivalent; credits pool at account-level ("liquid credit pool") and can be applied across projects/orgs. Prepay term must be in contract and is non-refundable but transferable within the same corporate entity.

Overage mechanics & stair-step model (monthly):
- Overage billed on actual usage beyond monthly commit. Overage rate = list rate * 1.10 for first 50% above commit (penalty band to discourage small under-commit increments).
- For 50% - 200% overage, overage rate steps down to list rate (1.00x) as usage demonstrates sustained demand — we cap the highest multiplier at 1.25x.
- If sustained overage for 3 consecutive months, we propose moving to an adjusted commit with retroactive true-up (crediting the customer for overage multipliers already paid up to agreed revised commit).
- Burst allowance: Dedicated plans include a monthly burst pool (configurable, default = 20% of commit capacity) that does not count against overage until exhausted.

Billing & true-up: monthly invoices with Net 30. Quarterly reconciliation (true-up) with option to annualize commits for discount protection. Unused committed credits do not auto-roll beyond 90 days unless a rolling-commit arrangement is in place.

SLA credits: availability/latency credits apply as percentage offsets to the next invoice (not as cash refunds). We can add stronger remedies in enterprise SOWs.

Marketplace / reseller adjustments: list prices shown are gross; if sold via marketplace/reseller, we net to Redwood after marketplace fees — we will show both lines on the quote.

I'll assemble these into the attached workbook and SOW draft for legal review.

Attachments: pricing-proposal-hs-v1.xlsx (workbook with tiered examples)

Hi Amit (and team),

Thanks for the clear list — please find our concise commercial response below and an attached sample pricing worksheet (pricing-proposal-hs-v1.xlsx) plus a short SOW template (sow-draft-hs.docx) showing Dedicated/Private deltas. TL;DR: we meter total tokens (prompt + generated), offer account-level prepay with a 10% bonus, and use a protective stair-step overage model with burst allowances on Dedicated.

1) Metering unit
- Redwood meters total tokens (prompt + generated). Billed granularity = per 1,000 tokens on invoices. This is consistent across Hosted API and Dedicated; Dedicated includes reserved GPU capacity semantics (burst pools apply before overages).

2) Commit mechanics
- Commits are quoted as monthly committed token volumes with an option to annualize for pricing protection. Commits are applied account-wide and can be allocated to projects/orgs via our Console.
- Unused commit credits: expire after 90 days by default; customers may opt into a rolling-commit addendum that allows longer carry-forward.
- True-up cadence: quarterly reconciliation by default; annual true-up available if annualizing commits.

3) Prepay / credits (Liquid Credit Pool)
- Option to prepay for 6+ months of committed usage and receive a 10% bonus of redeemable credits ("liquid credits").
- Credits live at the account level and can be consumed by any sub-organization under the same legal entity. They are non-refundable but transferable inside the corporate account.
- Credits can be applied to token consumption and to Reserved Capacity fees (pro-rated per month).

4) Overage mechanics & stair-step bands
- Overage is charged on actual tokens above monthly commit. Billing bands: first 0-50% over monthly commit = 1.10x list, 50%-200% over = 1.00x list (we step down to discourage repeated small under-commits but allow sustained usage to normalize), >200% = 1.25x list (exception band — we will require commit renegotiation).
- Dedicated plans include a configurable monthly burst allowance (default 20% of commit). Bursts consume the burst pool first and do not trigger overage until exhausted.
- Sustained overage for 3 months triggers an operational review and a proposal to re-baseline commit levels; prior overage multipliers are reconciled during true-up.

5) Discounts & marketplace sales
- Quoted list rates are gross. If transacted via a marketplace or reseller, Redwood shows both the gross list and the net Redwood-recognized amount after marketplace fees. Contracted discounts apply to list price; marketplace/reseller fees are handled as a separate line-item.

6) Billing & invoicing
- Monthly invoices, Net 30 default. Currency = USD (other currencies available via addendum). Quarterly reconciliation and an annual true-up option for annualized commits.

7) SLA credits
- SLA credits are applied as invoice offsets per the SLA schedule in the SOW. For enterprise SOWs we can negotiate cash-remedy schedules instead.

Attachments: pricing-proposal-hs-v1.xlsx (sample pricing worksheet with tiered examples)
sow-draft-hs.docx (SOW template showing Dedicated & Private deltas)
